text:
maria: Heads-up — after rolling the 6ms batch_window into canary cluster A, we saw a couple of p99 tail spikes on short seq (<= 64). Anyone else seeing this?
jonah: saw one alert earlier, haven't dived in. can you paste the repro and any profiler output?
maria: repro command: `wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --script shortseq.lua http://canary-a.internal/generate`
jonah: ok running now. can you share the runtime flags we used for the canary?
maria: flags: `batch_window_ms=6`, `coalesce_jitter_ms=1`, `token_budget_target=1536`, `max_batch_tokens=8192`
alex: quick note — kernel auto-fallback logs show a few "fallback_to_generic_kernel" entries around the same timeframe. might be related to small-batch path hitting an unoptimized codepath.
kevin: +1. if kernel falls back, per-token overhead goes up nontrivially for tiny batches. that amplifies tail latency when batching timers align badly.
maria: attaching profiler snippet (flame-ish, truncated):
```
user_dispatch -> 40%
KV_cache_lookup -> 18%
kernel_dispatch -> 12%
generic_attention -> 25%
other -> 5%
```
maria: note that generic_attention shows up only in the bad windows. in normal runs it's ~3%.
jonah: that pattern smells like KV cache eviction thrash. when micro-batches align, we evict/restore small KV pages, forcing the generic kernel that can't use the optimized KV path.
alex: agreed. also jitter=1ms is pretty tight. queueing jitter distribution might be too narrow, increasing collision probability.
kevin: suggestions: widen jitter to [2..8]ms, bump token_budget_target to 2048 for short-seq routes, and add a cheap KV-hit metric. can we A/B test those?
maria: I can run an A/B for canary-A vs canary-B. plan: canary-A keep current, canary-B: `coalesce_jitter_ms=3`, `token_budget_target=2048`, same batch_window=6. run for 2h.
jonah: i'll add a quick histogram for kv_cache_evictions and kernel_fallbacks to the per-route dashboard. if we see eviction spikes align with p99, that's our smoking gun.
sre-bot: deploy canary-B started by maria at 2024-11-02T13:12:10Z — rollout 20% traffic.
ci-bot: perf_job/shortseq-canary-B queued (job id: 4827).
alex: micro-bench results from local stage (short run): baseline p50=18ms p95=62ms p99=120ms; jitter=3,p_target=2048 -> p50=19ms p95=58ms p99=88ms. small improvement on tail.
maria: nice. if A/B confirms, we can land in next patch. also want to instrument kernel-selection reason codes in request traces.
jonah: small patch suggestion: prefer optimized-kernel if kv_pages_in_cache >= 75% for the batch; measure impact. pseudo: `if kv_hit_ratio(batch) > 0.75 -> prefer_fast_kernel()`
kevin: that rule seems safe. add a guard to avoid thrashing decisions per-request (memoize per 10ms window).
maria: action items: 1) A/B run + dashboards (jonah) 2) add kv eviction + kernel fallback metrics (jonah/alex) 3) try jitter [2..8]ms + token_budget bump (maria) 4) add kernel-selection heuristic (alex)
jonah: i'll create the dashboard tiles and a short runbook note. tagging @kevin for review on the kernel heuristic.
kevin: will review tonight. if we see consistent tail reduction, we can push to prod with a gradual ramp and alert on kernel_fallback_rate > 0.5%.
maria: thanks folks. I'll post results in ~3h. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks, gl hf. :rocket:
jonah: observed correlation already in first 30m: kv_evictions spiked at rollout boundaries — looks promising for the hypothesis.
sre-bot: canary-B reached 60% traffic at 2024-11-02T14:05:03Z (auto-step).
ci-bot: perf_job/shortseq-canary-B finished: summary -> p99 improvement ~28% (raw), full logs at http://ci.internal/jobs/4827/logs
maria: logging the outcome: canary-B improved p99 on short sequences by ~25-30%. we've paused further rollout until kernel-selection patch lands. will follow up with PR links. :white_check_mark:
